meta.topic: People on the ground and aboard ship, Oahu, 7 December 1941 (with pre-attack and aftermath vignettes)
meta.timeConvention: Hawaii local time (UTC-10:30) on 1941-12-07 unless the record carries a different 'date'/'dateEnd' (ISO). Tokyo time = Hawaii + 19h30m.
meta.positionConvention: Decimal degrees WGS84, west longitude negative. Ship positions are berth centres derived from the project anchors (Arizona Memorial 21.3649,-157.9500; Utah Memorial 21.3688,-157.9624; quay F-5 21.3622,-157.9534) along a Battleship Row axis of about 050/230 true with about 231 m between berths. Everything else is an estimate from chart memory: read 'posConfidence' and 'posUncertaintyM' before rendering, and prefer resolving people by place.shipId / place.baseId against the project's ship and airfield geometry datasets.

fields.dateEnd: ISO date of tEnd when different
fields.count: number of people visibly involved (null when unknown; see countNote)
fields.animTags: controlled vocabulary for the animator: stand_ranks, salute, raise_flag, play_instruments, run, man_gun, fire_mg, fire_rifle, fire_pistol, pass_ammo, swim, swim_burning_oil, jump_overboard, walk_hull, climb_line, cut_hull, drive_vehicle, fire_hose, carry_wounded, boat_rescue, wave_caps, takeoff, crash, phone, watch, shelter, treat_wounded, push_aircraft
fields.confidence: high = primary/official record or several independent accounts agree; medium = one good secondary source or memoir; low = single anecdotal source, or time/place/count is my estimate

meta.verificationNote: Direct page fetching was blocked in this environment (history.navy.mil, wikipedia.org and others did not resolve). Facts were checked through web-search result summaries plus prior knowledge of the standard literature (Lord, Prange, Arakaki & Kuborn, Cressman & Wenger, action reports). Anything a search could not confirm is marked in 'note' and listed in the dossier's Uncertainties section.

place.detail: Flight decks of Akagi, Kaga, Soryu, Hiryu, Shokaku and Zuikaku about 230 nmi north of Oahu, steaming east into the wind and pitching heavily
place.posBasis: approximate launch area quoted in secondary sources; use the carrier dataset

who.name: Mitsuo Fuchida
who.role: Strike leader, observer in Akagi B5N2 AI-301

who.name: Chuichi Nagumo
who.role: Commander, First Air Fleet, on Akagi's bridge

who.name: Minoru Genda
who.role: Air staff officer on Akagi's bridge

vignettes.countNote: 183 aircraft of the first wave got airborne in about 15 minutes; several hundred deck and maintenance crew per carrier lined the deck edges
actions: deck crews line the deck edges, island and gun galleries
launch officer swings a green lamp in a circle; chocks are pulled and handlers run clear
crews wave caps and arms and shout 'banzai' as each aircraft rolls down the pitching deck
a senior maintenance petty officer hands Fuchida a white hachimaki, which he ties over his flying helmet
fighters launch first, then level bombers, torpedo planes and dive bombers; formations circle and depart south about 06:20
vignettes.dress: Aircrew: brown cotton flight suits, kapok life vests, fur-lined leather helmets, white hachimaki. Deck crews: white or khaki working uniforms and soft caps. Officers on the bridge in dark blue.
vignettes.outcome: First wave en route; second wave (167 to 171 aircraft depending on source) launched about 07:05 to 07:15.
vignettes.source: Fuchida, 'I Led the Air Attack on Pearl Harbor', USNI Proceedings Sept 1952; Prange, At Dawn We Slept; NHHC collection of captured Japanese launch photographs (crewmen cheering 'Banzai')
vignettes.note: The best-known cap-waving photographs are attributed to Shokaku/Zuikaku and may show the second wave. The hachimaki story is Fuchida's own postwar account, which Zimm and others treat with caution. 06:00 Hawaii = 01:30 8 Dec Tokyo; some sources give first take-off 06:10 to 06:20.

place.detail: Defensive sea area a few miles off the Pearl Harbor entrance buoys; No. 1 4-inch gun on the forecastle and No. 3 gun on the starboard side of the galley deckhouse
place.posBasis: estimate; the midget submarine wreck found in 2002 lies 3 to 4 miles off the entrance

who.name: William W. Outerbridge
who.role: Commanding officer, on his first patrol in command

who.name: Oscar W. Goepner
who.role: Officer of the deck who sighted the conning tower trailing USS Antares

vignettes.countNote: two gun crews, bridge team and depth-charge party; ship's company about 115, largely Naval Reservists from St Paul, Minnesota
actions: lookouts sight a small conning tower following the target-towing ship Antares toward the gate
general quarters; Outerbridge runs to the bridge from his cot in the chartroom
ship works up from 5 to 25 knots and closes to under 100 yards
No. 1 gun fires at 06:45 and misses over; No. 3 gun fires and hits the conning tower at the waterline
four depth charges rolled off the stern as the submarine passes under
voice radio report sent to Commandant 14th Naval District
vignettes.dress: Outerbridge in pyjamas and a Japanese-style kimono robe; gun crews in dungarees and whatever they slept in, with life jackets and old-pattern steel helmets
vignettes.outcome: Midget submarine sunk (hull found in 2002 with a shell hole at the base of the conning tower). The report reached the 14th Naval District duty officer about 07:12 and Admiral Kimmel about 07:40; no general alert followed.
vignettes.quote: We have attacked, fired upon, and dropped depth charges upon submarine operating in defensive sea area.
vignettes.source: USS Ward action report (NHHC); NHHC H-Gram 001; Lord, Day of Infamy
vignettes.note: Ward's report: attack started 06:40, fire opened 06:45. The fuller radio message is logged 06:53 (a first, vaguer one at 06:51); the action report itself says a voice dispatch went at 06:45. St Paul reservist detail and Goepner's role are from standard secondary accounts and were not re-verified by search.

place.detail: SCR-270B mobile radar (operating van, antenna trailer, generator truck) on Opana Point, about 532 ft above the north shore near Kahuku
place.posBasis: Opana Radar Site National Historic Landmark coordinates

who.name: George E. Elliott Jr.
who.role: Plotter and motorman, practising on the oscilloscope

actions: scheduled 04:00 to 07:00 watch ends; they keep the set on for practice because the breakfast truck is late
Elliott at the oscilloscope sees the largest echo either has seen, about 3 degrees east of north at 137 (136) statute miles
Lockard checks the set for a fault, then confirms
Elliott plots it on the overlay map and telephones the Information Center at Fort Shafter
they keep plotting as the echo closes: roughly 45 to 47 miles at 07:30, about 20 to 22 miles at 07:39, then it is lost in ground return from the hills
vignettes.dress: Army khaki or fatigue clothing (not specifically documented)
vignettes.outcome: Warning dismissed at the Information Center. The plot was later matched to the first wave's approach.
vignettes.source: Joint Congressional Committee hearings (Lockard, Elliott testimony); Wikipedia, 'Radar warning of Pearl Harbor attack'; NPS Opana NHL documentation
vignettes.note: First-contact range is given as 132, 136 or 137 miles in different retellings; 137 at 07:02 is the usual figure. Intermediate plot ranges vary by a few miles between sources.

place.detail: Aircraft Information Center (plotting table with balcony) at Fort Shafter
place.posBasis: Fort Shafter Palm Circle reference point; the Information Center building lay within a few hundred metres

who.name: Kermit A. Tyler
who.rank: First Lieutenant, US Army Air Corps (78th Pursuit Squadron)
who.role: Pursuit officer on only his second training shift, 04:00 to 08:00

vignettes.countNote: the plotters had gone to breakfast at 07:00; the room was otherwise empty
actions: McDonald takes Elliott's call at the switchboard, finds no plotters and walks to Tyler, who sits alone at the plotting table
Opana calls back; Tyler takes the handset and listens to Lockard
Tyler tells him not to worry
McDonald asks whether to recall the plotters or tell Wheeler; Tyler declines
vignettes.outcome: No alert. Tyler assumed the echo was a flight of B-17s due from California; he had heard KGMB playing music through the night, which usually meant a ferry flight was homing on it. Later inquiries cleared him.
vignettes.source: Joint Congressional Committee hearings (Tyler testimony); Wikipedia, 'Radar warning of Pearl Harbor attack'
vignettes.note: The first Opana call came a few minutes after 07:02; the Lockard-Tyler conversation is usually placed about 07:20.

place.detail: Opana site, then the road down to the company camp at Kawailoa, about 9 miles away
place.posBasis: Opana NHL coordinates; route not surveyed

vignettes.countNote: two operators plus the truck driver
actions: shut the set down when the echo merges with ground return
truck arrives about 07:45
ride down to camp for breakfast; on the way they pass a truckload of helmeted men heading up to the site
learn of the attack on arrival and realise what they tracked
vignettes.outcome: The Opana set was back on the air later that morning.
vignettes.source: Lockard and Elliott testimony and interviews; Lord, Day of Infamy
vignettes.note: Truck arrival time and the passing-truck detail come from later recollections.

place.detail: Airborne at about 3,000 m: deployment flare off Kahuku Point (07:40), 'To-To-To' abeam Waimea Bay (07:49), 'Tora Tora Tora' at 07:53 while skirting the west coast
place.posBasis: Waimea Bay, the point named in Fuchida's account for 07:49; estimate

vignettes.countNote: crew of the lead B5N; 183 aircraft following
actions: Fuchida slides back the canopy and fires one signal flare: surprise achieved, torpedo planes first
the fighters do not react, so he fires a second flare about ten seconds later
Takahashi reads two flares as 'surprise lost' and takes the dive bombers in ahead of the torpedo planes
Mizuki taps 'To, To, To' (charge) at 07:49
Mizuki sends 'Tora, Tora, Tora' (surprise achieved) to Akagi at 07:53
vignettes.dress: Brown flight suit, life vest, helmet with hachimaki; Fuchida said he wore red underclothing so blood would not show
vignettes.outcome: Attack order mis-sequenced: dive bombers hit Ford Island and Hickam at about 07:55, a minute or two before the first torpedoes.
vignettes.source: Fuchida (Proceedings 1952); Prange, At Dawn We Slept; Zimm, Attack on Pearl Harbor; Wikipedia, 'Mitsuo Fuchida'
vignettes.note: Times 07:40, 07:49 and 07:53 are consistent across sources. Flare colour is reported variously (dark blue 'black dragon' smoke, or green). Zimm disputes parts of Fuchida's narrative.

place.detail: Seaplane ramp, parking apron and Hangar 1 of Naval Air Station Kaneohe Bay; four PBYs moored in the bay
place.posBasis: estimate of the hangar/ramp area on the south side of Mokapu Peninsula

who.name: Men of VP-11, VP-12 and VP-14 (Patrol Wing One)

vignettes.countNote: several hundred sailors and a Marine guard detachment on the station; no verified figure
actions: duty watch and men at breakfast run to the ramp as Zeros strafe the parked PBYs
sailors drag burning flying boats apart by hand and with tractors
men pull .30 and .50 calibre guns out of PBY waist hatches and mount them on pipe stands, benches and vises
rifles and BARs are handed out at the armory; men fire from hangar doors and from utility trenches
boat crews go out to burning PBYs at their moorings
vignettes.dress: Dungarees, undress whites and skivvies; Marines in khaki
vignettes.outcome: By the end of the morning 27 of the 33 PBYs on station were destroyed and 6 damaged. 18 Navy men were killed; the NPS list also names two civilians under Kaneohe.
vignettes.source: Patrol Wing One action report (NHHC); MCBH 'K-Bay's unforgettable warriors'; Wenger, Cressman & Di Virgilio, 'No One Avoided Danger'
vignettes.note: Kaneohe was hit about seven minutes before Pearl Harbor (07:48). Later strikes: level bombers about 08:55 to 09:00 and Zero strafing to about 09:30. Navy dead are given as 17, 18 or 19 in different sources.

place.detail: Traffic pattern and ramp of John Rodgers Airport (today's Honolulu airport), between Honolulu and Hickam
place.posBasis: estimate of the 1941 civil field

who.name: Cornelia Fort
who.role: Flight instructor in an Interstate Cadet

who.name: Suomala (first name not found)
who.role: Student pilot practising take-offs and landings

who.name: Robert H. 'Bob' Tyce
who.role: Airport flying-service operator, killed by strafing

actions: a military-looking aircraft bores straight at the trainer; Fort grabs the controls and pulls up over it
she sees red discs on the wings and smoke rising over Pearl Harbor
lands, and she and the student run for the hangar as a fighter strafes the field
Tyce is hit and killed on the ramp
vignettes.outcome: Fort survived (killed in a 1943 ferrying accident). Two other light planes from the field did not return.
vignettes.source: Cornelia Fort's logbook and 1943 article 'At the Twilight's Last Gleaming'; PBS American Experience; NPS civilian casualty list
vignettes.note: Exact clock time is not recorded; just before 07:55. Spelling varies Tyce/Tice (NPS list: Robert H. Tyce, 38). The lost Cubs are usually said to have carried soldiers of the 251st Coast Artillery on a rented flight; not verified here.

place.detail: Signal tower on the Navy Yard water tank, and the fantail and bow of every ship in the harbor
place.posBasis: estimate of the Navy Yard signal tower

who.name: Signal tower watch
who.role: Hoist the Prep flag for the whole harbor

who.name: Colour details, buglers, bands and Marine guards

vignettes.countNote: 2 to 4 men at each flagstaff; a band of about 20 and a Marine guard on each battleship; a single bugler or whistle on small ships
actions: blue 'Prep' flag is run up on the signal tower at 07:55
colour details stand by the stern flagstaff with the folded ensign and at the bow with the jack
bands and Marine guards form two ranks on battleship fantails
at 08:00 Prep is hauled down, ensign and jack go up, bands play the anthem or buglers sound 'To the Colors'; everyone topside faces aft and salutes
vignettes.dress: Undress whites and white hats; Marines in khaki
vignettes.outcome: The first bombs and torpedoes fell while most ships were between first call and colours; several hoisted colours under fire.
vignettes.source: Lord, Day of Infamy; ship action reports (Nevada, Utah, Oglala and others)
vignettes.note: Generic harbor-wide routine; per-ship details differ.

place.detail: Boat traffic between Battleship Row, the hospital ship Solace, the Merry Point and fleet landings and the Ford Island ferry slip; church rigging on battleship fantails
place.posBasis: centre of the boat routes; not surveyed

who.name: Lawrence E. Ruff
who.role: Went by launch with Nevada's Catholic chaplain to Mass aboard Solace; returned by boat to help take Nevada out

vignettes.countNote: dozens of 50-ft motor launches, 40-ft motor boats, gigs and whaleboats on the water
actions: motor launches carry church parties, liberty parties and returning overnight-liberty men across the channel
working parties rig awnings, benches and a portable altar on battleship fantails for services after colours
once the attack starts the same boats turn to picking up swimmers
vignettes.dress: Liberty and church parties in clean undress whites; officers in service dress whites; boat crews in whites or dungarees
vignettes.outcome: Boats already in the water became the first rescue craft.
vignettes.source: HistoryNet, 'Lieutenant Lawrence Ruff survived attack aboard USS Nevada'; Lord, Day of Infamy; National WWII Museum, 'Routine in Paradise'
vignettes.note: Only the Ruff/Drinnan trip is individually documented here. Positions and numbers of other church and liberty boats are not recorded; render as generic traffic.

place.detail: Patrol Wing Two command center and radio room, Ford Island, with a window toward the seaplane ramp
place.posBasis: estimate near the surviving hangar/control tower group on the south-east side of Ford Island

who.name: Logan C. Ramsey
who.role: Operations officer / chief of staff, Patrol Wing Two

who.name: Patrick N. L. Bellinger
who.role: Commander Patrol Wing Two, ill in his quarters on Ford Island

vignettes.countNote: plus radiomen in the adjoining room
actions: Ramsey and the duty officer stand at a window discussing a PBY's report of sinking a submarine
a plane dives on the seaplane ramp; Ramsey takes it for a reckless US pilot and tries to read its number
he sees something black fall from it and the bomb bursts at Hangar 6
he runs across the hall to the radio room and orders a plain-language broadcast on all frequencies
vignettes.dress: Aloha shirt and slacks, having hurried in from his quarters (Prange); not re-verified
vignettes.outcome: Broadcast at 07:58; CINCPAC rebroadcast at 08:00. It is the message that told Washington and the fleet.
vignettes.quote: AIR RAID, PEARL HARBOR. THIS IS NOT DRILL.
vignettes.source: Ramsey testimony, Joint Congressional Committee; Prange, At Dawn We Slept; Defense Media Network, 'Pearl Harbor: The Attack'
vignettes.note: Wording is printed with or without the 'X' separator and as 'NO DRILL' / 'NOT A DRILL' in different sources.

place.detail: Seaplane ramp and Hangar 6 at the southern end of Ford Island
place.posBasis: estimate south-west of the surviving Hangar 37

who.name: Sailors of Patrol Wing Two squadrons and NAS Pearl Harbor

vignettes.countNote: no verified figure
actions: dive bombers put the first bombs of the Pearl Harbor attack into the ramp and Hangar 6 at about 07:55
men run from hangars and barracks and pull undamaged PBYs and utility planes clear of burning ones
machine guns are stripped from aircraft and set up on tripods, benches and vises on the ramp
others fire rifles and pistols
later the same men haul oil-covered survivors out of the water along the shore
vignettes.outcome: About half the aircraft on Ford Island were destroyed or damaged; station deaths were very few.
vignettes.source: Patrol Wing Two and NAS Pearl Harbor action reports (NHHC); Lord, Day of Infamy
vignettes.note: Group vignette; no individuals verified.

place.detail: Quarterdeck of minelayer Oglala, moored outboard of cruiser Helena at 1010 Dock
place.posBasis: estimate: about 650 m south-east of California's berth across the channel

who.name: William R. Furlong
who.role: Commander Minecraft Battle Force, senior officer afloat in the yard area

vignettes.countNote: Oglala's crew plus Helena's
actions: Furlong paces the quarterdeck waiting for breakfast and sees a bomb fall on the Ford Island ramp
the plane banks and shows the red disc; he shouts for general quarters
has the signal hoisted for all ships in harbor to sortie
07:57: a torpedo runs under Oglala and hits Helena; the blast opens Oglala's port side
tugs move Oglala astern of Helena; crew abandon and set up guns and first aid on the dock
Oglala rolls over against the dock about 10:00
vignettes.dress: Not documented for Furlong; crew in whites, dungarees and skivvies
vignettes.outcome: Oglala capsized with no deaths; Helena lost about 33.
vignettes.source: USS Oglala and Commander Minecraft Battle Force action reports (NHHC); Lord, Day of Infamy
vignettes.note: Sequence is from the action reports and Lord; the search could not confirm the exact signal wording.

place.detail: Fantail (main deck aft) of USS Nevada at quay F-8, the north-east end of Battleship Row
place.posBasis: Nevada's berth centre estimated 231 m beyond Arizona on the row axis, then about 90 m further to her stern

vignettes.countNote: 23 bandsmen plus leader and a Marine colour guard (guard size not recorded)
actions: band and Marine guard form two ranks on the fantail at 07:55
they notice planes diving at the far end of Ford Island and take it for a drill
at 08:00 McMillan gives the downbeat for 'The Star-Spangled Banner' as the ensign starts up
a torpedo plane that has just dropped at Arizona passes over the fantail; its rear gunner strafes, misses the ranks and shreds the flag
a second strafer splinters the deck; McMillan falters, picks up the beat, and the band finishes the anthem
on the last note everyone runs for cover and battle stations
vignettes.dress: Band and colour detail in whites; Marines in khaki
vignettes.outcome: Nobody in the formation was hit. Nevada's gunners were firing within minutes.
vignettes.source: Lord, Day of Infamy; Military.com, 'As Pearl Harbor Was Attacked, a Navy Band Finished The Star-Spangled Banner'; Record-Courier Nevada timeline
vignettes.note: The strafing detail rests on Lord's interviews; the ship's log confirms band and Marine guard assembled aft for 08:00 colours. Some retellings spell the name McMillian.

place.detail: Fantail of USS Arizona for colours, then the ammunition-handling spaces below the forward turrets
place.posBasis: Arizona Memorial anchor shifted about 90 m toward the stern (north-east)

vignettes.countNote: bandmaster plus 20
actions: band musters on the fantail with instruments for 08:00 colours
air-raid alarm and general quarters: they stow or drop instruments and run forward and below
at battle stations they pass powder and shells in the ammunition hoist area under the forward turrets
the forward magazines detonate about 08:06
vignettes.outcome: All 21 were killed. The other fleet bands voted them the 1941 'Battle of Music' trophy, since renamed for the Arizona band.
vignettes.source: ussarizona.org band history; US Pacific Fleet Band history page; Syncopated Times, 'The Saga of Navy Band 22'
vignettes.note: Sources differ on the station (under Turret I or Turret II) and on whether they died there or on the way. Whether colours were actually played on Arizona is not established. They did not compete on 6 December; they had qualified earlier and attended as spectators. Kinney's name is from memory of the casualty roll and was not confirmed by search.

place.detail: Quarterdeck and third-deck damage-control stations of USS West Virginia, outboard at F-6
place.posBasis: midpoint of the Arizona and F-5 anchors, offset about 32 m outboard (south-east)

who.name: Claude V. Ricketts
who.role: Began counterflooding on his own initiative

who.name: Garnett Billingsley
who.role: Worked the counterflood valves with Ricketts

who.name: John S. Harper
who.role: First lieutenant and damage control officer

vignettes.countNote: the call brought several hundred men up from below
actions: Brooks sees a blast toward Ford Island, takes it for an internal explosion on California and passes the word for the fire and rescue party
men pour up the ladders to topside moments before the first torpedoes hit the port side
the ship lists quickly to port
Ricketts and Billingsley crank open starboard counterflood valves; the list comes off and she settles upright on the bottom
vignettes.outcome: West Virginia did not capsize; 106 of her crew died.
vignettes.source: USS West Virginia action report and Ricketts's statement (NHHC); Lord, Day of Infamy; Prange
vignettes.note: NHHC narrative credits Harper with initiating counterflooding; Ricketts's own statement says he and Billingsley started it. Both acted. Billingsley's first name and rate are from secondary accounts.

place.detail: A topside machine-gun station on USS Maryland, inboard at F-5
place.posBasis: project anchor for quay F-5

actions: Short sits near his machine gun addressing Christmas cards
sees torpedo planes coming in over the Southeast Loch, loads and opens fire unordered
hits a torpedo plane that has just dropped at Oklahoma
vignettes.outcome: Credited by Maryland with one of the first aircraft shot down. Maryland lost 4 men.
vignettes.source: USS Maryland action report (NHHC); Lord, Day of Infamy
vignettes.note: The exact gun mount is not given in the sources I could check.

place.detail: USS Oklahoma, outboard of Maryland at F-5; she rolls to port, away from Maryland
place.posBasis: F-5 anchor offset about 32 m outboard

who.name: Jesse L. Kenworthy Jr.
who.role: Executive officer and senior officer aboard; ordered abandon ship

vignettes.countNote: roughly 1,300 aboard; 429 died
actions: first torpedoes hit the port side about 07:56; lights fail and the list grows with each hit
word is passed to abandon ship over the starboard (high) side
hundreds climb over the starboard rail and walk or crawl across the side plating and bilge as the hull turns under them
men slide into the oil-covered water, swim to Maryland and climb her lines and blisters; some join her gun crews
boats pick up swimmers under strafing
vignettes.outcome: Capsized through about 135 degrees in roughly 12 minutes; masts in the mud, starboard bilge and a propeller above water by about 08:08.
vignettes.source: USS Oklahoma action report (NHHC); NPS 'USS Oklahoma'; DANFS
vignettes.note: Capsize time is given between 08:06 and 08:10. DANFS counts 20 officers and 395 men killed or missing; the final toll is 429.

place.detail: A flooding second-deck compartment with a small porthole on the high (starboard) side
place.posBasis: Oklahoma berth estimate

who.name: Aloysius H. Schmitt
who.role: Catholic chaplain, who had said Mass that morning

vignettes.countNote: Schmitt and about 12 men he helped out
actions: trapped with a group as the ship rolls, he helps men one at a time through the porthole
starts through himself, sticks, and asks to be pushed back so the men behind can get out
keeps boosting men through until the compartment floods
vignettes.outcome: Schmitt drowned, the first US chaplain killed in the war. His remains were identified in 2016.
vignettes.medal: Navy and Marine Corps Medal, upgraded to Silver Star in 2017
vignettes.source: NPS 'USS Oklahoma'; Aleteia, 'Pearl Harbor Catholic chaplain went down with USS Oklahoma'; War History Online
vignettes.note: The number saved is given as 12 in most accounts.

place.detail: Inside main-battery turrets as the ship turns over
place.posBasis: Oklahoma berth estimate

vignettes.countNote: each in a separate turret crew
actions: abandon ship is ordered as the lights fail
each stays in his turret holding a flashlight on the escape route so the rest of the crew can climb out
vignettes.outcome: Both went down with the ship.
vignettes.source: Medal of Honor citations; DANFS 'Oklahoma'

place.detail: Target ship Utah at berth F-11 on the north-west side of Ford Island
place.posBasis: USS Utah Memorial anchor

who.name: Solomon S. Isquith
who.role: Senior officer aboard; ordered the ship abandoned

who.name: Peter Tomich
who.role: In charge of the boiler rooms

vignettes.countNote: about 500 aboard; 58 died
actions: men waiting to hoist colours on the fantail watch planes drop torpedoes
two torpedoes hit the port side at 08:01
the 6-by-12-inch timbers laid on deck as bomb-target sheathing break loose and slide, trapping men
Isquith orders all hands topside and over the starboard side; men walk up the rolling side and slide down the bottom
Tomich stays below ordering his men out and securing the boilers
mooring lines part and the ship rolls over at 08:12; survivors swim about 100 m to Ford Island and shelter in a pipeline trench under strafing
vignettes.outcome: Utah remains where she capsized, with most of her dead aboard.
vignettes.source: USS Utah action report (NHHC); Navy.mil, 'Remembering the USS Utah'; NPS
vignettes.note: Dead are given as 58 (Navy, NPS) or 64 in some lists.

place.detail: Upturned bottom of Utah
place.posBasis: USS Utah Memorial anchor

who.name: John B. Vaessen
who.role: Trapped in the bilge after keeping the lights on at the switchboard

vignettes.countNote: a handful of Utah volunteers and a party from USS Raleigh with a cutting torch
actions: survivors on Ford Island hear hammering from inside the hull
volunteers go back onto the bottom under strafing and answer the taps
a torch brought from Raleigh cuts a hole through the bottom plating
Vaessen is pulled out
vignettes.outcome: Vaessen was the only man cut out of Utah.
vignettes.source: USS Utah action report; USNI oral history index (Vaessen); Defense Media Network
vignettes.note: Time of release is not fixed in the sources I could check (later that morning). One account names the torch man as 'Bill Hill'; the action report credits Szymanski's party and Raleigh. Vaessen's Navy Cross is from memory and unverified.

place.detail: Light cruiser Raleigh at berth F-12, next north-east of Utah
place.posBasis: estimate about 230 m north-east of the Utah anchor along the shore

vignettes.countNote: ship's company about 450
actions: a torpedo hits the port side at 07:56 and the ship lists
Simons directs from the bridge in blue pyjamas
gun crews fire the 3-inch and 1.1-inch batteries
the crew jettison topside weight to stay upright: aircraft, catapults, torpedo tubes, boats, anchors
a party takes a cutting torch to Utah's hull; a barge is lashed alongside as a pontoon
vignettes.dress: Captain in blue pyjamas; many of the crew in skivvies
vignettes.outcome: Raleigh stayed afloat with no deaths.
vignettes.source: USS Raleigh action report (NHHC); Lord, Day of Infamy
vignettes.note: The pyjamas detail is Lord's and was not confirmed by search.

place.detail: Signal (flag) bridge and navigation bridge in Arizona's forward superstructure
place.posBasis: Arizona Memorial anchor shifted about 35 m toward the bow (south-west)

who.name: Douglas Hein
who.role: On the bridge with the captain; survived badly burned

vignettes.countNote: bridge and signal-bridge watch; number approximate
actions: air-raid alarm, then general quarters
Kidd climbs to the signal bridge; Van Valkenburgh runs from his cabin to the navigation bridge and telephones for reports
bombs strike aft and amidships
about 08:06 a converted 16-inch shell penetrates beside Turret II and the forward magazines detonate; the forward superstructure collapses into the fire
vignettes.dress: Not documented; both senior officers were in uniform
vignettes.outcome: Both were killed; neither body was recovered. Kidd's Naval Academy ring was found fused to the conning-tower bulkhead.
vignettes.source: USS Arizona action report and survivor statements (NHHC); National WWII Museum, 'Rear Admiral Isaac C. Kidd's Medal of Honor'
vignettes.note: Explosion time: 08:06 in most modern reconstructions, about 08:10 in the action report. 1,177 of the 1,512 assigned to the ship died.

place.detail: Quarterdeck (aft) of Arizona and the boats alongside her stern
place.posBasis: Arizona Memorial anchor shifted about 55 m toward the stern

who.name: Samuel G. Fuqua
who.role: First lieutenant and damage control officer; senior surviving officer aboard

vignettes.countNote: about 335 of the crew survived; perhaps 100 or more passed over the quarterdeck
actions: leaves breakfast in the wardroom, reaches the quarterdeck and orders the alarm
is knocked unconscious by a bomb that hits the quarterdeck by Turret IV
comes to and directs men with CO2 extinguishers and buckets; there is no water pressure
after the magazine explosion he steers burned and wounded men aft and into boats bound for Ford Island and Solace
orders abandon ship, leaves in the last boat and returns to pick swimmers out of burning oil
vignettes.outcome: The stern third of the ship stayed above water and burned for two days.
vignettes.source: Fuqua's statement and USS Arizona action report (NHHC); USNI Proceedings Dec 1991, 'Sam Fuqua and the Death of Arizona'
vignettes.note: Fuqua's own statement puts the abandon-ship order at about 09:00; many narratives imply 08:30 to 08:45. The citation speaks of his 'amazingly calm and cool manner'.

place.detail: Port anti-aircraft director platform on Arizona's foremast, across about 20 m of burning water to Vestal's deck
place.posBasis: between the Arizona anchor and Vestal's estimated berth

who.name: Joseph L. George
who.rank: Boatswain's Mate Second Class, USS Vestal
who.role: Threw the line and refused an order to cut it

who.name: Donald G. Stratton
who.role: Crossed, burned over 60 percent of his body

who.name: Lauren F. Bruner
who.rank: Fire Controlman Third Class, USS Arizona

who.name: Alvin Dvorak
who.rank: Boatswain's Mate Second Class, USS Arizona

vignettes.countNote: six men crossing plus George
actions: six burned men are trapped on the director platform above the fire
George throws a weighted heaving line; they haul over a heavier line and make it fast
each goes hand over hand along the line, roughly 20 m across and 14 m above the water
George refuses to cut the line until the last man is over
vignettes.dress: Arizona men in burned whites and skivvies
vignettes.outcome: All six reached Vestal; five survived the war.
vignettes.source: NPS 'Joe George'; NHHC memorials for Stratton and Bruner; Stratton, All the Gallant Men
vignettes.note: Distance is given as 65, 70 or 80 feet. The crossing has to fall between the magazine explosion and Vestal casting off (08:30 to 08:45). The names of the four men other than Stratton and Bruner were not returned by search and are from memory of Stratton's account.

place.detail: Mainmast secondary-battery director on Arizona, then the water between the ship and the fuel pipeline on the Ford Island shore
place.posBasis: between the Arizona anchor and the Ford Island shore about 80 m north-west

who.name: Alan Shapley
who.role: Just-relieved commander of Arizona's Marine detachment

who.name: Earl C. Nightingale
who.role: Pulled along by Shapley when his strength failed

vignettes.countNote: the Marine director crew; number approximate
actions: Marines climb the mainmast tripod to their director station under strafing; Simensen is hit on the ladder
after the magazine explosion Shapley orders them down
they are blown or jump into the water and swim for the pipeline through oil and debris
Shapley tows the exhausted Nightingale by the shirt to shore
vignettes.dress: Marines in khaki; Shapley reached shore with most of his clothes blown off
vignettes.outcome: 73 of Arizona's 88 Marines died.
vignettes.source: Cressman & Wenger, Infamous Day: Marines at Pearl Harbor (USMC History and Museums Division)
vignettes.note: Detachment figures are from the USMC monograph as I recall it.

place.detail: Repair ship Vestal moored port side to Arizona's port side at F-7, bow north-east; later Aiea Shoal
place.posBasis: Arizona anchor offset about 35 m outboard

vignettes.countNote: about 100 men were blown off Vestal's decks; ship's company roughly 600
actions: Young takes charge of the 3-inch anti-aircraft gun; two bombs hit Vestal about 08:05
Arizona's magazine blast blows Young and about 100 men overboard and snuffs out Vestal's fires
an officer on deck orders abandon ship and men start over the side
Young swims back, climbs aboard covered in oil and sends them back to their stations
the crew cut the mooring lines with axes; a tug takes the bow about 08:30 and Vestal gets under way at 08:45
anchors off McGrew Point at 09:10, then is run aground on Aiea Shoal about 09:50
vignettes.dress: Not documented; Young came back aboard soaked in oil
vignettes.outcome: Vestal saved; 7 killed.
vignettes.quote: Lads, we're getting this ship under way.
vignettes.source: USS Vestal action report (NHHC); DANFS 'Vestal'; Medal of Honor citation
vignettes.note: The quotation exists in several versions (another runs: 'Where the hell do you think you're going? ... Get back aboard ship!'). Accounts differ on who gave the abandon-ship order. Simple retellings say 'beached at 09:10'; DANFS distinguishes anchoring at 09:10 from grounding at about 09:50.

place.detail: Starboard side of the signal bridge, then the navigation bridge, of West Virginia
place.posBasis: West Virginia berth estimate shifted about 25 m toward the bow

who.name: Doir C. Johnson
who.role: Communications officer; fetched Miller to help

actions: Bennion directs the ship's defence from the open bridge
a fragment from a bomb that hits Tennessee's Turret II tears open his abdomen
he refuses to be carried below and keeps asking how the fight and the fires are going
the pharmacist's mate dresses the wound; officers and Miller move him to a sheltered spot and later up to the navigation bridge out of the smoke
he dies on the bridge about 08:30; fire then drives everyone off
vignettes.outcome: Bennion died at his post.
vignettes.source: USS West Virginia action report, enclosures (NHHC); NHHC biography of Doris Miller
vignettes.note: Time of wounding is approximate (shortly after 08:05). An NHHC summary places Miller's finding of the captain 'in the magazine area', which conflicts with the action report's bridge.

place.detail: From the junior officers' wardroom area to the central passage ('Times Square'), then the bridge and the .50-calibre machine guns just aft of the conning tower
place.posBasis: West Virginia berth estimate shifted toward the bow

who.name: Doris 'Dorie' Miller
who.role: Mess attendant; the ship's heavyweight boxing champion

who.name: Frederic H. White
who.role: Loaded a second gun alongside Miller

who.name: Victor Delano
who.role: Expected Miller to pass ammunition; found him firing

actions: Miller is collecting laundry when the alarm sounds; his battle station, an anti-aircraft magazine amidships, is already wrecked by a torpedo
he reports to 'Times Square' and is sent to the bridge to help move the wounded captain

White and Delano load two unmanned Browning .50-calibre anti-aircraft machine guns; Miller, never trained on the weapon, takes one and fires at low-flying planes for about 15 minutes until the ammunition is gone
he helps lift the captain to the navigation bridge, then carries wounded men through oil and water to the quarterdeck
abandons ship with the last group as fires take hold
vignettes.dress: Not documented (mess attendants normally wore whites)
vignettes.outcome: First Black American awarded the Navy Cross, presented by Admiral Nimitz aboard Enterprise on 27 May 1942. Killed aboard USS Liscome Bay in November 1943.
vignettes.source: USS West Virginia action report, enclosure H (NHHC); NHHC biography 'Doris Miller'; Wikipedia, 'Doris Miller'
vignettes.note: Whether Miller hit any aircraft is unknown. The abandon-ship time is approximate. Officer names (Johnson, White, Delano) are from the action report as I recall it; the search summary did not echo them.

place.detail: Fantail and stern of USS Tennessee, inboard at F-6, pinned against the quays by the sunken West Virginia
place.posBasis: midpoint between the Arizona and F-5 anchors

vignettes.countNote: no verified figure
actions: anti-aircraft crews fire through both waves
burning oil from Arizona drifts down on the stern; hose teams on the fantail play water on the oil and on blistering paint
the engines are run ahead at 5 to 10 knots for hours, with the ship still moored, so the propeller wash pushes the burning oil clear
vignettes.outcome: Stern plating warped by the heat; 5 killed.
vignettes.source: USS Tennessee action report (NHHC); DANFS 'Tennessee'
vignettes.note: End time is nominal: the fires alongside burned into the night.

place.detail: Third-deck passageways and anti-aircraft battery of USS California at F-3, the south-west end of the row
place.posBasis: estimate about 530 m south-west of the F-5 anchor on the row axis

who.name: Herbert C. Jones
who.role: Organised a hand-passing party for the anti-aircraft guns; mortally wounded by a bomb

who.name: Thomas J. Reeves
who.role: Passed ammunition by hand in a burning passage until overcome

who.name: Robert R. Scott
who.role: Stayed at the air compressor feeding the guns as the space flooded

who.name: Jackson C. Pharris
who.role: Set up a hand-supply train and dragged unconscious men from oil-flooded compartments

who.name: J. W. Bunkley
who.role: Commanding officer; ordered and then cancelled abandon ship

vignettes.countNote: ammunition parties of several dozen men
actions: two torpedoes hit about 08:05; the powered hoists fail
men form lines and pass anti-aircraft shells by hand up ladders from the magazines
a bomb about 08:45 bursts on the second deck among them
burning oil drifts down the row and wraps the stern; at 10:02 the captain orders abandon ship and men go over the side to Ford Island
at 10:15 the order is cancelled and they come back to fight fires and flooding
vignettes.outcome: California settled into the mud over three days; about 100 dead.
vignettes.medal: Medal of Honor (Jones, Reeves and Scott posthumous; Pharris survived)
vignettes.quote: Leave me alone! I am done for. Get out of here before the magazines go off.
vignettes.source: Medal of Honor citations; USS California action report and survivor statements (NHHC); National WWII Museum, 'USS California Medal of Honor Recipients'
vignettes.note: The quotation is Jones's as given in his citation. Scott's citation has him say: 'This is my station and I will stay and give them air as long as the guns are going.' The search could not echo either verbatim; both are as I recall the citation texts. Dead: 98 in the early report, 100 in common use, 104 to 105 in NPS lists.

place.detail: Quarterdeck, then the starboard anti-aircraft director high in Nevada's superstructure
place.posBasis: estimate 231 m north-east of the Arizona anchor on the row axis

who.name: Joseph K. Taussig Jr.
who.role: Officer of the deck for the forenoon watch and anti-aircraft battery officer

vignettes.countNote: director crew; approximate
actions: takes the deck at 07:45; a second boiler is already being lit off, which later lets the ship move
at the alarm runs up to the starboard anti-aircraft director
a projectile passes through his left thigh; the leg is shattered
refuses to be carried down and goes on controlling the battery from where he lies
is finally lowered from the director as fire climbs the superstructure
vignettes.dress: Service whites as officer of the deck
vignettes.outcome: Lost the leg; later retired as a captain.
vignettes.source: Navy Cross citation; Wikipedia, 'Joseph K. Taussig Jr.'; USNI Proceedings Aug 2005
vignettes.note: The 'second boiler' credit is traditional and was not confirmed by search.

place.detail: Forward dynamo room, deep in Nevada's hull, then the after dynamo room
place.posBasis: Nevada berth estimate; the ship is moving after 08:40

who.name: Donald K. Ross
who.role: In charge of the forward dynamo room

vignettes.countNote: after he ordered his men out
actions: smoke, steam and heat from a bomb hit make the forward dynamo room untenable; Ross orders his men out
does every job himself until he is blinded and passes out
is revived, goes back in to secure the room, then takes over the after dynamo room until he collapses again
returns to duty once more until ordered to leave
vignettes.outcome: Nevada kept electrical power throughout her sortie.
vignettes.source: Medal of Honor citation; USS Nevada action report (NHHC)
vignettes.note: Not visible from outside the ship; listed for narration.

place.detail: Mooring quays F-8 at Nevada's bow and stern, and the water between quay and ship
place.posBasis: Nevada berth estimate, shifted a few metres toward Ford Island

vignettes.countNote: line-handling party; size not recorded
actions: Hill gets onto the mooring quay under strafing with his line handlers
they throw the heavy lines off the bollards
as the ship starts to move away he dives in and swims back, and is hauled aboard
vignettes.outcome: Nevada under way at 08:40. Hill was killed about half an hour later (see nevada_sortie_and_grounding).
vignettes.source: Medal of Honor citation; NHHC Nevada commemoration remarks; Wikipedia, 'Edwin J. Hill'
vignettes.note: The citation says he led his men to the quays, cast off and swam back. NHHC notes that accounts are vague on how he reached the quay.

place.detail: Down the channel past Arizona, West Virginia and Oklahoma, round the south end of Ford Island past 1010 Dock and the floating drydock, to Hospital Point
place.posBasis: estimate of the Hospital Point grounding position (end of the track)

who.name: Francis J. Thomas
who.role: Senior officer aboard; commanded the sortie

who.name: Lawrence E. Ruff
who.role: Acted as navigator on the bridge

who.name: Edwin J. Hill
who.role: On the forecastle to let go the anchors

vignettes.countNote: about 1,500 aboard
actions: backs clear and heads down-channel without tugs, down by the bow from a torpedo hit
passing the burning Arizona, gun crews shield ready ammunition from the heat with their bodies; men on other ships cheer
second-wave dive bombers concentrate on her off 1010 Dock and score at least five hits forward
to keep the channel clear she is run aground at Hospital Point at 09:10
Hill and his forecastle party, trying to let go the anchors, are killed or blown overboard by bombs
about 10:30 to 10:45 tugs Hoga and YT-130 push her across to Waipio Point
vignettes.dress: Whites, dungarees and skivvies; flash-burn injuries were worst on bare skin
vignettes.outcome: The only battleship to get under way. Dead: 50 in the NPS table; 60 killed and 109 wounded in the commonly quoted total.
vignettes.source: USS Nevada action report (NHHC); NHHC photo essays 'USS Nevada during the Pearl Harbor Attack'; Warfare History Network, 'USS Nevada's Run to the Sea'
vignettes.note: Under way 08:40 (Nevada, Jarvis reports) or 08:50 (Tangier report). The Waipio move time is approximate. Thomas's Navy Cross is from memory.

place.detail: Yard tug YT-146: from the yard-craft berths near 1010 Dock to Vestal and Arizona, Oglala, Nevada at Hospital Point, then Battleship Row
place.posBasis: estimate of the starting berth near 1010 Dock and the drydocks

vignettes.countNote: crew size approximate
actions: under way within about ten minutes of the first bombs; picks two men out of the water
takes a line from Vestal and helps pull her clear of Arizona about 08:30
at 08:50 goes to the sinking Oglala and helps move her astern of Helena as Nevada steams past
about 09:10 pushes on the grounded Nevada's bow and plays her fire monitors on the forecastle fires
helps move Nevada to Waipio Point, then fights fires along Battleship Row, ending on Arizona, for 72 hours
vignettes.outcome: Commended by Admiral Nimitz. Preserved today at North Little Rock, Arkansas.
vignettes.source: Wikipedia, 'Hoga (YT-146)' (from the NHL nomination); Naval Historical Foundation, 'Pearl Harbor Survivor: Tugboat USS Hoga'
vignettes.note: The end time is nominal: 72 hours of continuous firefighting from the morning of 7 December. Times 08:30 (Vestal) and 08:50 (Oglala) are from the landmark nomination.

place.detail: Hospital ship Solace anchored in East Loch north-east of Ford Island; her launches work alongside Arizona and West Virginia
place.posBasis: estimate of berth X-4; not verified

who.name: John A. Keefer
who.role: Led a stretcher party aboard Arizona

who.name: Joseph A. Cunningham
who.role: Led a stretcher party aboard Arizona

who.name: Grace B. Lally
who.role: Dressing for church when the attack began; ran the wards

vignettes.countNote: two motor launches with crews and stretcher parties at first; more boats followed. 13 nurses aboard.
actions: two motor launches with stretcher parties leave for Arizona within minutes
the parties board Arizona's burning quarterdeck and carry out the wounded as her crew abandon ship
boat crews steer into burning oil off West Virginia and Arizona and haul swimmers aboard, some going over the side after them
first casualties come up Solace's gangway at 08:20 to 08:25; boats shuttle all morning
vignettes.dress: Hospital corpsmen and nurses in whites; boat crews in whites or dungarees. The ship was painted white with a green band and red crosses.
vignettes.outcome: Solace took well over a hundred casualties that day. 13 nurses and 13 corpsmen were later cited.
vignettes.source: USS Solace action report (NHHC); DANFS 'Solace'; health.mil, 'Crew Aboard Navy Hospital Ship Solace Saved Lives'
vignettes.note: An Army medical officer aboard, Eric Haakenson, filmed Arizona's explosion from Solace's deck. Captain's name and the berth are from memory.

place.detail: The strip of water between Battleship Row and the Ford Island shore and the channel off West Virginia and Arizona, covered with burning fuel oil
place.posBasis: between the Arizona and Tennessee berths

who.name: Boat crews of the battleships, Solace, destroyers and the Navy Yard
who.role: Motor launches, whaleboats, admirals' barges, gigs

who.name: L. M. Jansen
who.role: Brought garbage lighter YG-17 alongside West Virginia to fight fires

vignettes.countNote: dozens of boats; hundreds of swimmers
actions: men jump from burning ships and swim under the flames or through gaps in them
launches nose into the fire; bowhooks lean out and drag oil-black swimmers aboard by the arms
boats run to the Ford Island fuel pier and landings, unload and go back
survivors wade ashore on Ford Island and shelter in ditches and the pipeline trench
vignettes.dress: Swimmers in oil-soaked whites and skivvies
vignettes.outcome: Most of the men who survived from Arizona and West Virginia came off this way.
vignettes.source: USS Solace, West Virginia and Arizona action reports (NHHC); Lord, Day of Infamy
vignettes.note: Group vignette. The YG-17 detail is from memory of the commendations and unverified.

place.detail: Submarine Base piers on Southeast Loch, under the torpedo planes' run-in to Battleship Row
place.posBasis: estimate of the Submarine Base finger piers

vignettes.countNote: approximate
actions: torpedo planes come down Southeast Loch at masthead height past the piers
Tautog's men break out a .50-calibre gun and hit one, which crashes close off the pier
PT-boat sailors climb into their twin .50 turrets and fire; other sailors shoot rifles from the piers
vignettes.outcome: Tautog and the destroyer-minelayer Hulbert are each credited with a torpedo plane in the first minutes.
vignettes.source: Motor Torpedo Boat Squadron One action report (NHHC); Bulkley, At Close Quarters; DANFS 'Tautog'
vignettes.note: From memory of the reports; the search did not reach these details.

place.detail: Channel north-west of Ford Island, off the seaplane tender Curtiss and Pearl City
place.posBasis: estimate

who.name: William P. Burford
who.role: Commanding officer of the ready-duty destroyer

vignettes.countNote: destroyer's company
actions: Monaghan gets under way at 08:27
Curtiss sights a conning tower about 08:36 to 08:40 and opens fire; flag signals warn of a submarine in the harbor
the midget fires a torpedo at Curtiss and another at Monaghan; both miss
Monaghan rams it at speed about 08:43 and drops two depth charges, then slides onto a derrick barge before backing clear
vignettes.outcome: Midget submarine destroyed; its wreck was later used as fill at the Submarine Base.
vignettes.source: USS Monaghan action report (NHHC); National WWII Museum, 'A Very Busy Day: USS Monaghan'
vignettes.note: Sighting times 08:36 to 08:40 by source; ramming 08:43 to 08:44. Burford's decoration is from memory.

place.detail: Seaplane tender Curtiss moored off Pearl City, west of Ford Island; starboard boat crane
place.posBasis: estimate of berth X-22

who.name: Curtiss gun crews and damage-control parties

actions: a dive bomber hit by the ship's fire crashes into the forward starboard crane and burns at 09:05
at 09:12 a bomb strikes near the same crane and bursts below decks
hose parties fight the hangar and deck fires while the guns keep firing
vignettes.outcome: About 19 killed and nearly 60 wounded.
vignettes.source: DANFS 'Curtiss'; USS Curtiss action report (NHHC)
vignettes.note: Dead are given as 19, 20 or 21.

place.detail: Travelling crane on the rails beside Drydock No. 1, which holds Pennsylvania with destroyers Cassin and Downes ahead of her
place.posBasis: estimate of Drydock No. 1

vignettes.countNote: plus Pennsylvania's gun crews below him
actions: from his cab about 15 m up he sees the planes before the ship's crew, deep in the dock, can
runs the crane back and forth along the dock to spoil low-level runs
swings the boom to point at incoming aircraft; the gunners take to using it as a pointer
a bomb bursting on the dock about 09:06 wrecks the crane and stuns him
vignettes.outcome: Walters survived and was commended in Pennsylvania's report.
vignettes.source: USS Pennsylvania action report (NHHC); Lord, Day of Infamy
vignettes.note: From memory of Lord and the action report; the search did not return it. Pennsylvania's dead: 15 killed plus 14 missing in the action report, 18 in the NPS table.

place.detail: Navy Yard main gate, then the head of Drydock No. 1
place.posBasis: estimate of Drydock No. 1

actions: arrives to photograph the Marine gate guard for a Christmas card
without his camera permit he turns to helping instead and mans a fire hose on the burning destroyers in the drydock
later carries food and messages to the gun crews
vignettes.dress: His trademark pith helmet and work clothes
vignettes.outcome: Commended for firefighting at Drydock 1. His photographs of the aftermath are standard images of the attack.
vignettes.source: Tai Sing Loo, 'How I Happened to Be at Pearl Harbor'; DVIDS, 'Who is Tai Sing Loo?'; Wikipedia, 'Tai Sing Loo'

place.detail: Heavy cruiser New Orleans at Berth 16 in the Navy Yard repair basin, engines under repair and on shore power
place.posBasis: estimate of the repair basin

who.name: Edwin F. Woodhead
who.role: Officer in charge of the ammunition line

vignettes.countNote: ammunition line; size approximate
actions: shore power is lost: no lights and no ammunition hoists
men fire rifles and pistols until the guns are supplied
a line of sweating sailors passes 5-inch rounds by hand up from the magazines
Forgy, unable to hold services, walks the line slapping backs and encouraging them
vignettes.dress: Skivvies and dungarees; Forgy in uniform
vignettes.outcome: The phrase became the 1942 song title.
vignettes.quote: Praise the Lord and pass the ammunition.
vignettes.source: National WWII Museum, 'The WWII Origin of Praise the Lord and Pass the Ammunition'; Wikipedia article of the same title; USS New Orleans action report
vignettes.note: Early press credited another chaplain (Maguire); Forgy's authorship was established in 1942. Woodhead's first name and the berth number were not confirmed by search.

place.detail: Main gate, drydocks, 1010 Dock and the repair basin of the Pearl Harbor Navy Yard
place.posBasis: estimate of the yard's industrial centre

who.name: Civilian yard workmen
who.role: Shipfitters, welders, chippers, riggers, crane and locomotive operators

vignettes.countNote: a Sunday skeleton shift at first; thousands by afternoon
actions: workers drive and run in through the main gate against the outbound traffic, some hit by falling shells on the way from Honolulu
they man hoses on Cassin, Downes, Pennsylvania and Shaw, carry ammunition and rig power and air lines
shop gangs load compressors, chipping guns and torches into launches for the capsized ships
vignettes.dress: Work clothes, some in Sunday clothes; lunch pails
vignettes.outcome: Yard workers were among the civilian dead and wounded.
vignettes.source: Commandant 14th Naval District reports; Wallin, Pearl Harbor: Why, How, Fleet Salvage and Final Appraisal; NAVSEA shipyard history articles
vignettes.note: Group vignette.

place.detail: Parade ground of the Marine Barracks inside the Navy Yard
place.posBasis: rough estimate

who.name: Marines of the barracks and the 1st, 3rd and 4th Defense Battalions

vignettes.countNote: several hundred
actions: colour guard and field music are on the parade ground for 08:00 colours as the first planes pass
a bugler sounds Call to Arms; Marines fall out with Springfield rifles and fire from the parade ground
machine guns are set up on the parade ground and roofs within about 20 minutes; 3-inch guns later in the morning
the mess hall feeds survivors and the barracks become an aid station
vignettes.dress: Khaki shirts and trousers, field hats or garrison caps
vignettes.outcome: The barracks Marines claimed several aircraft and took few casualties.
vignettes.source: Cressman & Wenger, Infamous Day: Marines at Pearl Harbor
vignettes.note: Gun counts and timings are as I recall the monograph (8 machine guns by about 08:20, 13 later); verify before quoting.

place.detail: Naval Hospital Pearl Harbor at Hospital Point: nurses' quarters, lawns and wards
place.posBasis: estimate just inland of Hospital Point

who.name: Ruth A. Erickson
who.role: Ward nurse; left a detailed oral history

vignettes.countNote: about 30 nurses plus doctors and corpsmen; hundreds of patients
actions: nurses at breakfast in their quarters hear planes and see the red discs from the lanai
they run across the lawn to the hospital through falling fragments
the first patient reaches the dressing room at 08:25 with an open abdominal wound
burned men arrive by the truckload; nurses and corpsmen spray tannic acid from flit guns, give morphine and mark foreheads
a shot-down Japanese plane clips a hospital building and burns in the grounds
mattresses are laid on floors and lanais as beds run out
vignettes.dress: White ward uniforms and caps; corpsmen in whites
vignettes.outcome: The hospital recorded 546 casualties admitted and 313 dead brought in on 7 December.
vignettes.source: NHHC oral history, 'Pearl Harbor Attack, Lt. Ruth Erickson, NC, USN'; BuMed, 'Pearl Harbor Navy Medical Activities'
vignettes.note: First-patient time: 08:25 in the oral history, 08:20 in a later quotation. The 546/313 totals and the plane-crash detail are from memory of the BuMed account. Commanding officer's name unverified.

place.detail: Kimmel's quarters and the neighbouring lawn on Makalapa hill, overlooking Battleship Row from the east; then by car down to headquarters at the Submarine Base
place.posBasis: estimate of the Makalapa quarters

who.name: Vincent R. Murphy
who.role: Fleet duty officer, on the telephone

who.name: Mrs John B. Earle
who.role: Neighbour; wife of the 14th Naval District chief of staff

actions: about 07:40 Murphy phones the Ward report; Kimmel says he will come down and starts dressing, his golf with General Short forgotten
about 07:55 Murphy calls again: the signal tower reports an air raid, no drill
Kimmel runs out still buttoning his white jacket and stands on the Earles' lawn watching the torpedo planes
his car pulls up and he is driven to headquarters, arriving about 08:05 to 08:10
vignettes.outcome: Kimmel was relieved of command in mid-December 1941 (16 or 17 December, by source).
vignettes.quote: I knew right away that something terrible was going on, that this was not a casual raid by just a few stray planes.
vignettes.source: Prange, At Dawn We Slept; Kimmel testimony; Lord, Day of Infamy
vignettes.note: Mrs Earle remembered his face 'as white as the uniform he wore'. The search confirmed only that he was at his quarters and went to headquarters; lawn details and clock times follow Prange and Lord from memory.

place.detail: Second-floor office window of the Pacific Fleet headquarters at the Submarine Base, facing the harbor
place.posBasis: estimate of the headquarters building

actions: Kimmel stands at the window watching the fleet burn
a spent .50-calibre bullet comes through the glass and strikes him on the chest, leaving a smudge on his white jacket and a welt
he picks it up and speaks quietly to Curts
vignettes.outcome: He kept the bullet. Later that morning he replaced his four-star shoulder boards with two-star ones.
vignettes.quote: It would have been merciful had it killed me.
vignettes.source: Layton, And I Was There; Prange, At Dawn We Slept; Wikipedia, 'Husband E. Kimmel'
vignettes.note: The incident and words are well attested (wording varies: 'more merciful'). The clock time is my estimate: sources say only 'during the attack'. The shoulder-board story is from Layton and unverified here.

place.detail: Commandant's quarters and the 14th Naval District headquarters in the Navy Yard
place.posBasis: rough estimate

who.name: John B. Earle
who.role: Chief of staff, who had relayed the Ward report about 07:15

actions: Bloch, at his quarters, has been waiting for confirmation of the Ward report
the explosions begin; he goes to district headquarters
orders yard tugs and craft to fight fires and rescue swimmers, and reports the raid by telephone and radio
vignettes.outcome: District craft (tugs, garbage lighters, ferries) worked through the day on fires and rescue.
vignettes.source: Joint Congressional Committee hearings (Bloch, Earle testimony); Commandant 14th Naval District report
vignettes.note: Thinly documented at the level of movement and time; written from general knowledge of the testimony. Do not render specific actions without further checking.

place.detail: Commanding general's quarters on Palm Circle, Fort Shafter
place.posBasis: Fort Shafter Palm Circle reference point

actions: Short hears explosions toward Pearl Harbor and takes them for a Navy exercise
steps outside and sees smoke
a few minutes after 08:00 his chief of staff reports that it is the real thing
he orders all units to Alert No. 3 (occupy battle positions) and moves to the forward command post in Aliamanu Crater
vignettes.outcome: The Army had been on Alert No. 1 (anti-sabotage): aircraft bunched, ammunition boxed and anti-aircraft batteries out of position. Short was relieved in mid-December (16 or 17 December, by source).
vignettes.source: Short testimony, Joint Congressional Committee; Conn, Engelman & Fairchild, Guarding the United States and Its Outposts, ch. VII
vignettes.note: Times (08:03 report, alert orders by about 08:10) are as I recall Short's testimony; the search did not confirm them.

place.detail: Hangar line, Hawaiian Air Depot and the apron where bombers stood in close rows; control tower on the hangar line
place.posBasis: estimate of the hangar line; Hickam geometry was not verified in this research

who.name: William E. Farthing
who.role: Base commander, in the control tower waiting for the B-17s

vignettes.countNote: ground crews and guards on the line
actions: Farthing watches aircraft diving on Pearl Harbor from the tower and takes them for Navy planes
dive bombers and strafing fighters hit the depot, hangars and parked B-18s, B-17s and A-20s
ground crews run to the line, taxi or tow aircraft apart and pull men from burning planes
one man fires a .30-calibre gun from the nose of a parked B-18 until the plane burns under him; another carries a machine gun to a hangar roof
vignettes.dress: Khaki, mechanics' coveralls, some in pyjamas or underwear
vignettes.outcome: Roughly half of Hickam's bombers were destroyed or damaged in the first wave.
vignettes.source: Arakaki & Kuborn, 7 December 1941: The Air Force Story, ch. V; 15th Wing fact sheet
vignettes.note: The unnamed-gunner episodes are from the Air Force history as I recall it.

place.detail: Central mess hall of the consolidated barracks 'Hale Makai' (today's Pacific Air Forces headquarters building)
place.posBasis: estimate of the barracks; not verified

who.name: Enlisted men at breakfast and mess staff

vignettes.countNote: 35 killed by the one bomb; several hundred were in or near the hall
actions: men sit at breakfast in the mess hall at the centre of the multi-wing barracks
a bomb comes through the roof and bursts among the tables
survivors run out onto the parade ground; others carry casualties to the hospital on doors and mattresses
the barracks is strafed and bombed again in the second wave
vignettes.outcome: 35 killed in the mess hall. The building still carries its bullet scars.
vignettes.source: NPS, 'Hickam Field'; National Register nomination for Hickam Field; Arakaki & Kuborn
vignettes.note: The barracks housed about 3,000 (NRHP) to 3,200 men. The clock time of the mess-hall hit is not fixed in the sources I could check; first wave is the usual statement.

place.detail: Parade ground in front of the burning barracks, around the flagpole, and the adjoining ball field
place.posBasis: estimate; not verified

vignettes.countNote: the open ground filled with men from the barracks
actions: men pour out of the barracks onto the open parade ground
a group sets up a machine gun in the open and fires at strafers; a Zero kills them, and a second crew that takes over the gun is killed almost at once
others fire Springfield rifles and pistols standing or kneeling in the open
the base flag on the parade-ground flagpole is shot to ribbons but stays up
vignettes.dress: Khaki, fatigues, underwear, a few in old-pattern helmets
vignettes.outcome: The tattered flag was kept and is displayed in the headquarters building.
vignettes.source: Arakaki & Kuborn (photograph: gun emplacement on the parade ground in front of burning barracks); Air Force survivor accounts (af.mil, pacaf.af.mil)
vignettes.note: Individuals in this scene are not named in the sources I could check.

place.detail: Bomb craters near the barracks and between the hangars; a sandbagged gun in front of Hangar 5
place.posBasis: estimate; not verified

who.name: Wilbur K. Hunt
who.role: Set up machine guns in fresh bomb craters

who.name: Raymond Perry
who.role: Manned the gun emplacement in front of Hangar 5

who.name: Howard Marquardt
who.role: Manned the gun emplacement in front of Hangar 5

who.name: Guardhouse prisoners
who.role: Freed when a bomb hit the guardhouse; joined Hunt's gun crews

vignettes.countNote: about a dozen guns; approximate
actions: between the waves Hunt draws .50-calibre machine guns and sets them up in bomb craters
prisoners freed from the bombed guardhouse run over and help mount and man them
the guns engage the second wave's level bombers and strafers
after the raid a sandbagged emplacement is built in front of Hangar 5
vignettes.outcome: Hunt received the Silver Star.
vignettes.source: Arakaki & Kuborn, ch. V; Silver Star citation (Military Times Hall of Valor); PACAF photo captions
vignettes.note: Search confirmed Hunt's Silver Star and the Perry/Marquardt emplacement. The 'twelve guns in craters' and guardhouse-prisoner details are from memory of the Air Force history.

place.detail: Hickam runways and tower; other B-17s put down at Haleiwa, Bellows and the Kahuku golf course
place.posBasis: estimate of the Hickam tower area; not verified

who.name: Truman H. Landon
who.role: Led the 38th Reconnaissance Squadron flight; landed at Hickam

who.name: Richard H. Carmichael
who.role: Led the 88th Reconnaissance Squadron flight; landed at Haleiwa

who.name: Raymond T. Swenson
who.role: His B-17C was set on fire by strafing and burned in two on the Hickam runway

who.name: William R. Schick
who.role: Flight surgeon in Swenson's aircraft, mortally wounded

who.name: Frank P. Bostrom
who.rank: First Lieutenant, US Army Air Corps
who.role: Chased by fighters; landed on the Kahuku golf course

who.name: Robert H. Richards
who.rank: First Lieutenant, US Army Air Corps
who.role: Landed downwind at Bellows and ran off the short strip

who.name: Gordon A. Blake
who.role: Talked the bombers down from the Hickam tower

vignettes.countNote: 12 B-17s (four B-17C, eight B-17E) with reduced crews; unarmed, guns packed in grease, low on fuel after 14 hours from California
actions: the bombers arrive in ones and twos in the middle of the first wave
Zeros attack them in the pattern; American gunners fire at them too
Swenson's aircraft is hit as it lands, its flare box ignites and the fuselage burns through; the crew run for the grass under strafing and Schick is hit
others land at Hickam between attacks or divert: two to Haleiwa, one to Bellows, one to the golf course at Kahuku
vignettes.outcome: One B-17 destroyed, three badly damaged. Schick died of his wounds.
vignettes.source: Arakaki & Kuborn, ch. IV and Appendix D; HistoryNet, 'Pacific Tramps'
vignettes.note: Sources disagree on the landing tally (one account has six at Hickam, another puts one at Wheeler) and on arrival times (first arrivals a few minutes after 08:00). Blake's role, Swenson and Schick are from the Air Force history as I recall it.

place.detail: Hickam fire station and the hangar line; Honolulu engines came in by the main gate from Kalihi, Palama and downtown
place.posBasis: estimate; not verified

who.name: William L. Benedict
who.role: Badly wounded early in the attack

who.name: Frederick Kealoha, Moses Kalilikane, John A. Gilman, Solomon H. Naauao Jr., Patrick J. McCabe, George Correa

vignettes.countNote: three Honolulu engine companies plus surviving Hickam firemen; approximate
actions: Hickam's fire station is bombed and its trucks wrecked in the first minutes
the alarm reaches Engine 6 in Kalihi at 08:05; Engines 4 and 1 follow under mutual aid
the companies arrive to find a hangar and aircraft burning and the water main broken; they draft from a flooded bomb crater
the second wave catches them in the open about 09:00: three firemen are killed and six wounded
the survivors keep the lines going with soldiers on the hoses
vignettes.dress: Dark fire-department uniforms and leather helmets
vignettes.outcome: The six wounded received Purple Hearts in 1944, the only civilian firefighters so decorated; Pang's was awarded posthumously in 1984.
vignettes.source: National Fallen Firefighters Foundation, 'Memorial Monday: Pearl Harbor'; Hawaiian Journal of History article on the Honolulu Fire Department; Firehouse, 'Dec. 7, 1941: A Day of Infamy and Fire'
vignettes.note: Arrival times are not recorded in the sources found. Company assignments of the two captains and the full spelling of the wounded men's names are from memory (the search returned garbled spellings).

place.detail: Station Hospital, Hickam Field, a new 30-bed building near the main road
place.posBasis: estimate; not verified

vignettes.countNote: about 7 medical officers, 7 nurses, 40 enlisted men, plus volunteer wives
actions: casualties arrive within minutes on trucks, doors and litters; the porch and lawn fill with wounded
Fox assists in surgery, gives anaesthesia and dresses wounds while bombs fall close by
she organises officers' and NCOs' wives as volunteers to make dressings
the worst cases are sent on to Tripler by ambulance and truck
vignettes.dress: White nurses' uniforms; medics in khaki
vignettes.outcome: Fox became the first woman awarded the Purple Heart (October 1942); as she had not been wounded it was replaced by the Bronze Star in 1944.
vignettes.medal: Purple Heart, later replaced by Bronze Star
vignettes.source: National Women's History Museum, 'The Bravery of Army Nurse Annie G. Fox'; Air Force Medical Service, 'Medical Memories from Dec. 7, 1941'
vignettes.note: Lane's name is from the Air Force medical history as I recall it.

place.detail: Hangar line and apron on the north side of the field; the tent area between Hangars 2 and 3
place.posBasis: estimate from the airfield reference point

who.name: Howard C. Davidson
who.rank: Brigadier General, US Army Air Corps

who.name: Enlisted men of the 15th and 18th Pursuit Groups
who.role: Many asleep in tents beside the hangars

vignettes.countNote: about 90 fighters parked wingtip to wingtip in rows on the apron
actions: 25 dive bombers put about 35 bombs into the hangars and barracks, then return with fighters to strafe the rows of P-40s and P-36s
men asleep in the tent area are caught in the strafing and the fires; tents burn
ammunition stored in a hangar cooks off
survivors run to push undamaged fighters clear of the burning rows
senior officers run from their quarters in pyjamas
vignettes.outcome: Wheeler had no anti-aircraft guns, trenches or shelters. 33 killed and 75 wounded in the usual count.
vignettes.quote: I could even see the gold in their teeth.
vignettes.source: NPS, 'Wheeler Field'; Arakaki & Kuborn, ch. VI; Lord, Day of Infamy
vignettes.note: Start time: 07:51 in the NPS timeline, about 08:02 in the Air Force history. Casualties also appear as 38 killed and 59 wounded, or 37 killed, 6 missing and 53 wounded. The quotation is Flood's, from Lord, from memory. Lord also has Davidson's ten-year-old twin daughters collecting spent cartridge cases on the lawn; unverified.

place.detail: From the Wheeler officers' quarters by road about 16 km to the grass strip at Haleiwa, then in the air over Ewa and Wheeler
place.posBasis: Haleiwa Fighter Strip coordinates (destination). Start point Wheeler about 21.488,-158.037 (estimate).

vignettes.countNote: plus Haleiwa ground crews
actions: after a dance and an all-night poker game at Wheeler they are woken by the bombing
Taylor phones Haleiwa to have two P-40s fuelled and armed while Welch fetches Taylor's new Buick
they pull on their tuxedo trousers and drive about 16 km at up to 100 mph, strafed on the way
they take off about 08:30 without orders, with .30-calibre ammunition only, and attack dive bombers over Ewa
they land at Wheeler about 09:00 to rearm and take off again as the second wave strafes the field; Taylor is wounded in the arm and leg and Welch shoots a fighter off his tail
vignettes.outcome: Welch was credited with four aircraft and Taylor with two. Both received the Distinguished Service Cross.
vignettes.source: Arakaki & Kuborn, ch. IV; Wikipedia, 'Kenneth M. Taylor'; History.com, 'Heroes of Pearl Harbor: George Welch and Kenneth Taylor'
vignettes.note: Distance is given as 10 or 11 miles. The 08:30 take-off is the Air Force history's figure as I recall it; the search found no clock time. Whose Buick it was varies by account. Other 47th Squadron pilots (Brown, Rogers, Dains, Webster, Moore) also drove to Haleiwa and flew; Dains was shot down and killed by friendly anti-aircraft fire.

place.detail: Wheeler flight line, then the air over Kaneohe Bay
place.posBasis: estimate of the Wheeler hangar line

actions: Rasmussen straps a pistol belt over his pyjamas and helps push undamaged P-36s clear
armourers load the guns by hand as the four taxi out between the waves
Sterling hands his wristwatch to the crew chief, saying he will not be back
they take off about 08:50 and fight a formation of Zeros over Kaneohe; Sterling is shot down into the bay
Rasmussen brings his fighter back with about 500 holes, no brakes or rudder and a shot-off tail wheel
vignettes.outcome: Sanders and Rasmussen each credited with a kill. Rasmussen is the 'pyjama pilot' of the Air Force Museum diorama.
vignettes.source: Arakaki & Kuborn, ch. IV; Military Times, 'The pajama pilot over Pearl Harbor'
vignettes.note: Take-off time approximate.

place.detail: Infantry, artillery and engineer quadrangles next to Wheeler Field
place.posBasis: rough estimate of the quadrangle area

who.name: James Jones
who.role: Later author of From Here to Eternity; at breakfast in the company mess

who.name: Stephen G. Saltzman
who.role: Fired a BAR at a low-flying plane

who.name: Lowell V. Klatt
who.role: Fired a BAR at a low-flying plane

vignettes.countNote: 24th and 25th Infantry Divisions were quartered here
actions: men at Sunday breakfast hear the explosions at Wheeler and crowd into the quadrangles
fighters pass down the quads strafing on their way to and from Wheeler
supply rooms are opened; soldiers fire rifles and BARs from the ground and the barracks roofs
Saltzman and Klatt run outside with BARs and fire at a plane pulling up over power lines; it crashes beyond the building
vignettes.outcome: A few casualties at Schofield; the divisions moved to their beach positions that morning.
vignettes.source: Prange, December 7, 1941: The Day the Japanese Attacked Pearl Harbor; James Jones, WWII; 25th Infantry Division Association
vignettes.note: The Saltzman/Klatt episode is from Prange (confirmed via a secondary citation). Jones's recollection is a memoir.

place.detail: An exposed section of the aircraft parking ramp near the VP-14 hangar, NAS Kaneohe Bay
place.posBasis: estimate of the hangar and ramp area

who.name: John W. Finn
who.role: Chief in charge of the squadron's ordnance

vignettes.countNote: with ordnancemen feeding him ammunition
actions: woken at his quarters about a mile away, he drives to the hangars, keeping to the speed limit until a plane with red discs passes him
takes over a .50-calibre machine gun from the squadron painter and mounts it on a movable tripod instruction stand
drags the stand into the open on the ramp for a clear field of fire
fires at strafing and bombing aircraft through both waves, for more than two hours, while hit repeatedly by fragments and bullets
leaves for first aid only when ordered, then comes back to supervise re-arming of the surviving planes
vignettes.dress: Not documented; he dressed in a hurry
vignettes.outcome: Wounded many times (he counted 21 wounds). He is generally credited with hits on Lieutenant Iida's fighter.
vignettes.medal: Medal of Honor (presented by Admiral Nimitz aboard Enterprise, 15 September 1942)
vignettes.source: Medal of Honor citation; NHHC, 'The Warrior of Kaneohe'; Wikipedia, 'John William Finn'
vignettes.note: The citation says 'painfully wounded many times'; the figure 21 is Finn's own. The presentation date appears as 14 or 15 September 1942. His was the earliest Medal of Honor action of the US war, since Kaneohe was struck first.

place.detail: Low over the armory and hangars, then a hillside road cut near the married officers' quarters; a marker stands on Reed Road
place.posBasis: rough estimate of the marker area

who.name: Fusata Iida
who.role: Fighter division leader from Soryu, second wave

who.name: Sands
who.role: Stood outside the armory firing a BAR at the diving fighter

vignettes.countNote: plus the sailors firing at him
actions: Iida's nine Zeros strafe the station; his fighter is hit and trails fuel
he signals his wingmen, pointing to himself and then at the ground, turns back alone and dives at the armory with guns firing
sailors at the armory door stand and fire rifles and BARs at him
the fighter passes over and smashes into the hillside about a kilometre from the hangars
vignettes.outcome: Iida was killed. The station's sailors buried him with their own dead, with honours, on 8 December.
vignettes.source: MCBH, 'Fusata Iida'; Pacific Wrecks A6M2 3277; Lansdale, 'The Lost Pearl Harbor Attack Aircraft' (j-aircraft.com); Lord, Day of Infamy
vignettes.note: Clock time is my estimate inside the second-wave strafing window. Before take-off Iida had told his pilots he would crash a crippled aircraft into a worthy target. Sources disagree on his target (hangar or armory). The Sands episode is from Lord and unverified.

place.detail: Ewa Mooring Mast Field: officers' mess, guardhouse, tent camp and the rows of parked aircraft
place.posBasis: airfield reference coordinates

who.name: Carlo A. Micheletto
who.role: Fought fires, then fired a rifle from behind a pile of lumber; killed

vignettes.countNote: several hundred Marines; 47 or 48 aircraft parked in the open
actions: Ashwell, in the officers' mess at 07:55, sees torpedo planes heading for Pearl Harbor and fighters coming down over the Waianae Range; he runs to the guardhouse to sound the alarm
Zeros strafe the parked rows at a few metres' height for about 25 minutes
Marines run from the tents and fire back with rifles, pistols and Thompson guns, standing in the open
others drag machine guns from damaged planes or try to pull aircraft out of the fires
the station fire truck and ambulance are shot up on the field
vignettes.outcome: Almost every aircraft at Ewa was destroyed or damaged. Four Marines died.
vignettes.source: Cressman & Wenger, Infamous Day: Marines at Pearl Harbor; Warfare History Network, 'Embattled Marines at Air Station Ewa'; American Rifleman, 'Remember Pearl Harbor: The Men and the Guns'
vignettes.note: The NPS list names four Ewa Marines: Lutschan, Turner, Lawrence and Micheletto. The ambulance took more than 50 hits (USMC photo caption).

place.detail: The road about a mile from the field, then the Ewa command post
